One expression per line, and tabular clauses, graded against the current text; all four clean. Deciding sentence for every head and clause line: "A line reads in one pass when it holds a selection and the one expression that selection produces." (SKILL.md, the rule's first sentence), with "Count expressions, not calls or brackets" for nested-call lines. Constructs that exercised it: every do: head holds one expression (haiku-1 lines 60, 63, 113, 123, 125; haiku-2 lines 70, 73, 94, 96, 106; sonnet-1 lines 69, 121, 123, 133; sonnet-2 lines 69, 117-119, 121, 133, 143), including nested calls such as haiku-1 line 63 def match(path), do: TinyRouter.__match__(unquote(Macro.escape(compiled)), path). Sequences and nested constructs sit below their heads, under "What asks for a second line is not a second call but a second expression ... Those go on the lines below the head": the get macro bodies, the __before_compile__ bodies, __match__/2 (two statements, then a fn holding a case), haiku-1 expand_path!/2 and expand_handler!/2 (binding then if), sonnet-2 __match__/2 lines 104-107. Compact case clauses inside fns and for bodies (haiku-1 lines 74-75 and 107-108, haiku-2 lines 84-85, sonnet-1 lines 102-103 and 115-116) each hold one pattern and one expression, so the first sentence passes them without the table paragraph; the for-body cases are also tables (one mapping, one fallback row). sonnet-2 find_route/2 lines 124-130 breaks a case whose :error clause continues the recursion, the shape "Clauses are not a table when they do different kinds of work, as when one row returns a finished value and the next continues the computation" names. Not counted under this rule: the one-line pipelines of haiku-1 line 51 and haiku-2 line 66 (no selection on the line; graded under the pipeline rule) and the one-line fn of sonnet-1 line 65 and sonnet-2 line 62, whose fn head shares its line with one expression, {path, handler}; its layout is the captures rule's sentence and is listed there under other_violations.

Do: rule, graded against the current text; all four clean. Constructs and deciding sentences: one-expression bodies including nested calls and tuples, "A `do:` body is one expression on the head's line: a literal, a tuple, a field read, a comparison, or a call, nested or not." (every do: line listed above; e.g. sonnet-2 line 117 defp parse_segment(":"), do: raise(ArgumentError, "route param needs a name, got \":\"")). fn and capture sentences: no fn and no argument-carrying capture in any do: body; the fns sit in block bodies or bindings and sonnet-2's &parse_segment/1 (line 112) is a bare capture inside a pipeline block. if sentence ("when both carry a computation of their own, write `do ... end`"): no one-line if in any run; haiku-1 lines 83-87 and 93-97 and haiku-2 lines 39-41 and 43-48 are blocks. for sentence ("A `for` always takes `do ... end`"): exercised by haiku-1 lines 105-110 and sonnet-1 lines 113-118, both blocks. Multi-clause sentence ("A multi-clause function need not be a table to keep `do:` clauses"): sonnet-2 parse_segment/1 lines 117-119 keeps three do: clauses. Mix sentence ("each block clause set apart with a blank line; when the clauses are one parallel group, give them one form"): haiku-1 bind/3, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 match_segments/3 each keep a base clause and a fallback on do: and set the two recursive block clauses apart; the clauses end, recurse and fail, different kinds of work, so they are not held to be one parallel group, and the block clauses join to 104-163 characters, so they could not be do: lines. Head's-line sentence: no do: body on a line of its own. Every one-expression do ... end block joins to more than 98 characters (haiku-1 100-102 121, 115-117 104, 119-121 126; haiku-2 90-92 121, 98-100 163, 102-104 119; sonnet-1 90-92 130, 108-110 106, 125-127 140; sonnet-2 135-137 144), and the guard-wrapped or guarded blocks (sonnet-1 72-74 and 129-131, sonnet-2 77-79, 85-88 and 139-141) are not counted, as before.

Pipeline rule, graded against the current text. Deciding sentence: "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short". haiku-1 line 51 and haiku-2 line 66 write the __before_compile__ pipeline with two steps after env.module on one line (the same line as in 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-29-check haiku-1). sonnet-2 writes both its pipelines on separate lines starting with the value (lines 57-60 and 109-113). sonnet-1 has no |> and writes the same two steps as the nested call at line 64, which "or become a nested call when there are only two" allows, so it is clean rather than not exercised.

Other changed rules outside the list: the captures rule's layout paragraph from 551e3ab ("A `fn` that binds names takes the room its names earn: the body goes on the line after the `->`") decides sonnet-1 line 65 and sonnet-2 line 62, both one-line fns binding {path, handler, _segments}; listed under other_violations. Make polymorphism explicit (library-design.md, unchanged sentence "Check input types at the public boundary with guards or patterns, so a bad argument fails with a FunctionClauseError naming your function") is listed for haiku-1 and haiku-2, as 2026-10-29-check did for haiku-1: MyApp.Router.match(123) fails with FunctionClauseError in String.split/3; in both sonnet runs it fails in the generated match/1, which has an is_binary guard.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace, one scratch Mix project per run (the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex, plus real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules). sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 report alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime) and alias MyApp.UserHandler (runtime); they call Macro.expand_literals with {:routes, 0} and {:call, 2}. haiku-1 calls Macro.expand(handler, env) and haiku-2 calls Macro.expand_literals(handler, __CALLER__) with no function in the env; both report alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile) and alias MyApp.UserHandler (compile). All four compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3).

Bad-declaration checks: each project loaded with mix run, then Code.compile_string compiled one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All eight fail while the router compiles: haiku-1 and haiku-2 with CompileError (nofile:3: route path must be a string, got: 123; route handler must be a module name, got: "not a module") raised during macro expansion; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 with ArgumentError from the @doc false __define__/3 that get's quote calls.

Format: all four pass mix format --check-formatted, matching result.json. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 put parentheses on the two get calls; sonnet-1 kept them bare and delivered a .formatter.exs with locals_without_parens: [get: 2] and export, and passes with it.

Reads: all four read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md before writing tiny_router.ex. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 used one Read call per file; sonnet-1 read SKILL.md with Read and both reference files with cat in one Bash call.
